reports.title: Juan Martin: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: At national level, as part of our mission to build an NHS fit for the future, we will make sure mental health care is delivered in the community wherever possible - through new models of care and support available for those who are struggling - so that more people are prevented from needing to go into hospital.
promises.summary: Expand community mental health care to reduce hospital admissions

promises.quote: The Trust (SWLStG) fully acknowledges the concern regarding insufficient bed capacity in London and the reason why the Coroner has cause to raise these concerns.
promises.summary: Acknowledge concern and commit to improving bed capacity

concerns.quote: bed capacity remains an ongoing problem and has not been resolved
genuine risk of future deaths directly connected to a shortage of mental health bed spaces in London
concerns.hazard: future deaths due to mental health bed shortage

concerns.quote: no suitable bed was identified until approximately after 15:00 on 12 April 2022

reports.title: Tracey Ostler: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Lack of Psychiatric Hospital Beds in Surrey and arrangements for detaining patients assessed to require Mental Health Act section in the Emergency Department of Epsom General Hospital
concerns.hazard: detention of psychiatric patients in emergency department without Mental Health Act section

concerns.quote: Training for Paramedics to undertake Capacity Assessments
concerns.hazard: inadequate paramedic capacity assessment for mental health crises

concerns.quote: The Trusts policy on Mental Capacity is being reviewed to improve articulation of how to assess mental capacity in life threatening circumstances. It is not yet available. I regarded the current policy as inadequate and remain concerned about this because I have not been able to review the revised document
concerns.hazard: absence of reviewed Mental Capacity policy for life threatening decisions

concerns.quote: Ms Ostler suffered from a severe Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder, this was a longstanding diagnosis, and the effects were well known to her mental health team. She was placed in the community on a Positive Risk Taking Plan. She presented a continuous and serious risk to herself in the community and was prone to impulsive acts of self harm. Ambulances were frequently required to attend her home after such acts. The disorder impacted her ability to make capacitous decisions about her own care
concerns.hazard: lack of multi-agency safeguarding for high-risk personality disorder

concerns.quote: I have not been provided with any Protocol between the services to ensure safety planning in these circumstances that would ensure that front line paramedics are made aware that they are dealing with a seriously unwell mental health patients who is at high risk living in the community
concerns.hazard: absence of safety protocol for high-risk mental health patients

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient psychiatric/mental health bed capacity leading to patients being held in emergency departments while awaiting admission. The earlier report focuses on London-wide bed shortages, while the later report concerns Surrey-specific delays in the ED of Epsom General Hospital.
links.earlier_quote: The Matron in Acute and Urgent Care confirmed bed capacity remains an ongoing problem and has not been resolved.
links.later_quote: patients with psychiatric presentations, who are assessed to require compulsory admission under the Mental Health Act 1983, are detained without being under section in the emergency department awaiting psychiatric beds.
links.promise_quote: The Trust (SWLStG) fully acknowledges the concern regarding insufficient bed capacity in London and the reason why the Coroner has cause to raise these concerns.

followups.summary: The Trust acknowledged concerns about insufficient bed capacity in London, but no source confirms a specific action was taken or a timescale provided.
